references.text: Jesus later confirms that they are from below and he is from above, and that they will die in their sins if they do not believe that he is who he says he is. This explains the Jews' misunderstanding of his words about going where they cannot follow.

Jesus repeats the same theme to the disciples: 'Where I am going, you cannot come now,' which shows that the Jews' reaction in 8:22 was a logical consequence of a repeated claim about an insurmountable divide.
Here Jesus says to the Jews: 'Where I am going, you cannot come,' and they interpret it in the same way as in 8:22, by asking if he is going to the scattered Greeks.
